answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity with slashing. Each agent must bond tokens to join, and peers check its work; if a cluster of fake accounts colludes, their bonds are burned. Cheap sybils may wander in, but each one costs real capital, like building huts on a knoll above a lagoon where every extra hut needs its own lumber. Because rewards scale with verified useful output rather than account count, splitting one stake across many identities gains nothing and only multiplies slashing risk.
